data.incumbent: A homegrown billing system, built by a guy who left; effectively doing nothing / status quo

evidence.excerpt: Their VP of Product, Owen, had wanted to rebuild billing for a while.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Trigger was a long-standing wish by Owen, not a discrete event.

evidence.excerpt: The billing system is homegrown, built by a guy who left, and every pricing change takes them a quarter.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Describes the incumbent and the pain: a quarter per pricing change.

evidence.excerpt: He reached out to us.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Inbound from Owen.

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one big thing.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep says no single trigger event.

evidence.excerpt: He wanted it done before they launched a new pricing tier, but the tier didn't have a date either.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Soft deadline tied to an undated pricing tier; no forcing date.

evidence.excerpt: The CFO, I guess? Diane.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep hedges on who made the final call.

evidence.excerpt: They missed their number in Q3 and she put a hold on all new vendor projects.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Q3 miss led to a freeze on all new vendor projects; learned via Owen.

evidence.excerpt: So I don't know that you'd say she decided against us. She decided against everything.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep frames it as a blanket freeze, not a loss to us.

evidence.excerpt: Owen told me. I never spoke to her.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Everything about Diane and the freeze is secondhand via Owen.

evidence.excerpt: No. Owen said he'd bring her in at the end.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: The final decider was never in a meeting; deferred to the end.

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one. It was us against doing nothing.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: No competitor; status quo was the alternative.

evidence.excerpt: Owen never looked at anybody else, as far as I know.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Hedged with 'as far as I know'.

evidence.excerpt: Toward the end Owen started asking for things for finance.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Customer questions shifted toward finance needs late in the cycle.

evidence.excerpt: "do you have something that shows payback?"
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen asked for payback evidence; the word is payback.

evidence.excerpt: That started maybe a month before the freeze.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Timing is hedged with 'maybe'; later given as 'about a month'.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the billing demo. Changing a price in a few clicks, trials, proration.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: The demo drew a reaction.

evidence.excerpt: "that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen's reaction to the demo, framed in roadmap time.

evidence.excerpt: His engineers were into it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Engineers reacted positively to the demo.

evidence.excerpt: I don't know that anything got silence.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep hedges on silence, then names revenue framing.

evidence.excerpt: We only ever talked to product and engineering.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: No contact with finance during the deal.

evidence.excerpt: I guess the revenue framing.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep's guess on what got silence.

evidence.excerpt: "we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen rejects our revenue-growth framing in favor of roadmap tax.

evidence.excerpt: The freeze email. Before that we were in procurement. Well, we'd sent paper.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Freeze arrived by email; paper sent, with a self-correction from 'in procurement'.

evidence.excerpt: I sent him the ROI deck. The general one, with the study.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Responded to payback request with a generic ROI deck.

evidence.excerpt: "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen needed a customer-specific number to win Diane's approval.

evidence.excerpt: We were going to set up a session to build one. Then Q3 closed.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: The session to build their number was planned but never happened.

evidence.excerpt: About a month.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Gap between payback ask and the freeze.

evidence.excerpt: The number. Their own. What the homegrown system costs them.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Main thing the customer asked for that we couldn't show.

evidence.excerpt: he mentioned once that some landlord subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it. We never added it up.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Cost lead (failed-card lapses) was mentioned but never quantified.

evidence.excerpt: He also asked about migration. Moving the existing subscriptions over without asking landlords for their card details again, and whether they could do it in stages.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Migration questions: no re-collecting cards, staged approach.

evidence.excerpt: "we don't touch billing before renewal season."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Pikeview engineering lead
evidence.note: Engineering lead's timing constraint on billing changes.

evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Migration doc existed; Owen wanted a reference customer. No follow-through stated.

evidence.excerpt: Owen's was "a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen's phrase for the problem.

evidence.excerpt: "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Diane (via Owen)
evidence.note: Diane's funding rule, relayed through Owen.

evidence.excerpt: Owen said finance saw it as a nice to have.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Owen
evidence.note: Owen reported finance's view; 'nice to have' is not in quotes here.

evidence.excerpt: For Owen, yeah. For Diane, no.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep's read on urgency differing between Owen and Diane.

evidence.excerpt: I don't think anyone told her what it was costing.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep's assumption that Diane never saw the cost.

evidence.excerpt: It's timing. It'll come back next year.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep predicts return; no evidence offered.

evidence.excerpt: I don't think there was anything we could have done.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Renee
evidence.note: Rep's conclusion, in tension with the unmet payback number.

contradictions.what: Rep says nothing could have been done, yet Owen said he needed a customer-specific number for Diane, which was never built, and Diane likely never saw the cost.
Rep says 'it's timing' and it will return next year, while also saying Diane froze everything; the engineering lead's renewal-season constraint also suggests other timing barriers.
Rep names Diane as final decider but never spoke to her, she was in no meeting, and all knowledge of her is via Owen.
Rep says nothing got silence, then names the revenue framing, which Owen explicitly rejected.
Rep says no single trigger and no deadline, yet the evaluation ran into a Q3 close and a freeze.
Rep says they were in procurement and had sent paper, but the ROI session needed to justify the deal was never held.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Rep first said she didn't know anything got silence, then guessed revenue framing, which Owen had pushed back on.

dodges.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
dodges.what: Rep hedged ('I guess?'), reframed the freeze as not a decision against us, and later admitted never speaking to Diane.

dodges.question: When did you first feel this wasn't going to close? What happened right before?
dodges.what: Rep answered with the freeze email and a self-correction about procurement; right-before details emerged only after a follow-up.

dodges.question: Anything else?
dodges.what: Rep closed with 'timing' and 'nothing we could have done', contradicting the unmet payback number described earlier.

outcome_signals.what: The deal ended in a freeze, not a clear loss: Diane put a hold on all new vendor projects after the Q3 miss. The rep says it was not decided against us.
Paper had been sent but nothing signed; the ROI session was planned and never held.
No competitor; the alternative was doing nothing. This was a no-decision, not a competitive loss.
Rep expects it to return next year but offers no evidence; she believes nothing could have changed the outcome.
